note: Recorded clarifying questions for the sample (hand-authored).

questions.question: When a DBT payment fails in PFMS (for example the account is not Aadhaar-seeded or is closed), what should happen to the application?
questions.whyItMatters: Without a defined failure flow, failed payments stay unresolved and the vendor will treat re-payment as a change request.
suggestedAnswers: Notify the student by SMS to correct bank details within 30 days; re-initiate in the next weekly batch
Notify the institution to follow up with the student
Re-initiate automatically after the account is seeded
questions.defaultAssumption: The student is notified by SMS to correct bank details within 30 days, and payment is re-initiated in the next weekly PFMS batch.

questions.question: Can a student appeal against rejection by the District Social Welfare Officer, and to whom?
questions.whyItMatters: An appeal adds a role, a workflow state and a timeline, and is expected under the Right to Service Act.
suggestedAnswers: Appeal to the Director, Social Welfare within 30 days
Appeal to the District Collector within 30 days
No appeal; the student may re-apply once
questions.defaultAssumption: The student may appeal to the Director, Social Welfare within 30 days of rejection, to be decided within 15 working days.

questions.question: Should records from the paper process be migrated, such as last year's beneficiaries who will apply for renewal?
questions.whyItMatters: Migration affects effort, the renewal flow and the go-live plan.
suggestedAnswers: Migrate 2025-26 beneficiaries as a master for renewal
questions.defaultAssumption: Only 2025-26 beneficiaries are migrated as a beneficiary master for renewal; pending paper applications are not migrated.

questions.question: To whom should an application be escalated when the institution or the District Social Welfare Officer misses the 15-day timeline?
questions.whyItMatters: Escalation rules are needed to keep within the 30-day Right to Service timeline.
suggestedAnswers: Institution delay to DSWO; DSWO delay to Joint Director, Social Welfare
All delays to the Director, Social Welfare
questions.defaultAssumption: Institution delays are escalated to the District Social Welfare Officer, and DSWO delays to the Joint Director, Social Welfare.

questions.question: When does the renewal window open, and should last year's beneficiaries get a prefilled renewal application?
questions.whyItMatters: Defines the renewal trigger and which data is reused.
suggestedAnswers: Window opens 1 July; prefilled renewal for last year's beneficiaries
Same window as fresh applications, no prefill
questions.defaultAssumption: The renewal window opens on 1 July and last year's beneficiaries receive a prefilled renewal application.

questions.question: How long should applicant data be retained after the final payment?
questions.whyItMatters: Retention is mandatory under the DPDP Act and affects storage and archival design.
suggestedAnswers: Until the course ends plus 1 year
questions.defaultAssumption: Applicant data is retained for 8 years after the last payment and then anonymised.

questions.question: Which actions must be recorded in the audit trail, and who may view it?
questions.whyItMatters: Determines logging scope and access to sensitive records.
suggestedAnswers: All status changes and data edits; State nodal officer can view
questions.defaultAssumption: All status changes, data edits and exports are logged, and the audit trail is viewable by the State administrator.
